cover.hook: Ottawa just committed to 500 megawatts of sovereign AI compute — and $1 billion to bring AI inside federal departments.
cover.sub: Plus Anthropic's cryptographic model proof, OpenAI flexing the power grid, COP31, and AI funding open in Northern Ontario now.

reelSub: Five AI and funding moves NWO can't ignore this week.
storySub: What this week's AI and funding news means for a Northwestern Ontario business.

items.title: Budget 2026: Ottawa puts $1B into AI-first federal services
items.body: Budget 2026 creates Digital Transformation Canada and a $1B Government Transformation Fund. Canada also commits to 500 MW of sovereign AI computing for Canadian companies — terms still to come.
items.tease: Next: a cryptographic proof of which AI model answered you.
items.reelLine: Canada's Budget 2026 commits $1 billion to federal AI and creates Digital Transformation Canada.

items.title: Anthropic open-sources a proof of which AI model answered you
items.body: FlashProve uses a zero-knowledge proof (zkSNARK) to verify model identity without revealing the weights. It targets the risk of a provider swapping in a cheaper model. Research prototype — not production-ready yet.
items.tease: Next: who pays when AI drains the power grid.
items.reelLine: Anthropic released FlashProve — an open-source cryptographic proof of which AI model answered a request.

items.title: OpenAI will flex power during grid stress — Ontario is writing the rules
items.body: OpenAI's Grid Protectors Program commits future campuses to cut power during strain events. Ontario's grid operator projects data centres at 8.6% of provincial demand by 2050. The Data Centre Playbook puts connection costs on developers.
items.tease: Next: Canada's climate credibility at COP31.
items.reelLine: OpenAI announced its Grid Protectors Program. Ontario's data centre rules are coming this fall.

items.title: COP31 opens; Canada's delegation faces rollback scrutiny
items.body: Climate talks run November 9–20 in Antalya, Turkey. Canada promoting methane cuts but eliminated the carbon price, cancelled the oil-and-gas emissions cap, and paused the coal export ban. What is committed here shapes NWO resource-sector rules next.
items.tease: Next: AI adoption funding open in Northern Ontario now.
items.reelLine: COP31 opened November 9. Canada's climate credibility is on the table.

items.title: FedNor RAII is open for Northern Ontario AI projects
items.body: Rolling intake, no fixed deadline. Three streams: AI adoption, commercialization, ecosystem. National program expanded to $700M. Worth a call to FedNor before the fiscal year runs out.
items.reelLine: FedNor's RAII is open for Northern Ontario businesses — no fixed deadline, three streams.

summary.title: Federal AI is becoming funded infrastructure
summary.body: Budget 2026 moves Canada from AI strategy to AI spend — $1 billion and a new central body — while technical accountability tools and grid rules catch up around the edges. For NWO, it means the AI operating environment is changing at every level: policy, power, and funding.
